# Coder task 007 — put the paper's placement and eviction rules back

**Opened 2026-09-16.** Thinker → coder. Do not edit this file; write everything in `REPORT.md`.
Starting point: tag **`sbc-start-2026-09-16`** (`8ed66ea`, task 005 commits 0–1). Branch `sbc-sampling`.
Task 005 commits 2 and 3 are **deliberately skipped** — do not build them.

**Why this task exists:** [../../performance/fix-plan-follow-the-paper-2026-09-16.md](../../performance/fix-plan-follow-the-paper-2026-09-16.md)
(the decision doc — read §0, §1 and §2 before you start) and
[../../performance/why-sbc-loses-2026-09-15.md](../../performance/why-sbc-loses-2026-09-15.md) (the diagnosis).

---

## 0. Before you start

- Read `CLAUDE.md` top to bottom, then the two documents above.
- **Simulate only through `make run-binary` / `run_sbc.sh`** — a bare `$SIM` call omits `+dramsim` and
  false-fires the BankedStore shadow assert at cycle 27141. CLAUDE.md explains this at length.
- **No new control register.** See §3. Build the behaviour directly and keep the RTL simple.
- Nothing here may elaborate hardware when `enableSetBalancing = false`, and the **SBC-off build must
  stay bit-identical** — that is how you prove you broke nothing outside the feature.
- Counter rules from 005 §2.2 still bind: **MSHR pulses are added with `PopCount`, never OR-ed.**
  This task extends that rule to two places 005 did not cover (§2).
- Plain-language words used here: a **guest line** is a line that was moved out of its own set and now
  sits in a partner set (`displaced` in the RTL). A **home line** sits in the set it belongs to.
  **S** = source set, **D** = destination set, **K** = ways per set.

---

## 1. What is wrong today, in one paragraph

A migration may only overwrite one of D's **home** lines, never an older guest
([MSHR.scala:1468-1470](../../../design/craft/inclusivecache/src/MSHR.scala#L1468-L1470)); D's own misses
take a guest only when no home way is left at all
([Directory.scala:216-226](../../../design/craft/inclusivecache/src/Directory.scala#L216-L226)); and a
pairing never ends ([SetBalanceUnit.scala:263-271](../../../design/craft/inclusivecache/src/SetBalanceUnit.scala#L263-L271)).
Together those three rules drive every destination set to **1 home line and 15 guests**, which is 47% of
the cache parked — measured twice on the board at 64 KB (477 and 483 of 1,024 lines, task 005 REPORT
"Board runs") and once at 256 KB (1,903 of 4,096). The paper has none of these rules: its eviction is by
recency, a displacement takes D's LRU line whatever it is, and the pair breaks when D's last guest goes.

Guests are **not** the problem in themselves — the same board runs show ~74 secondary hits per parked
line. The problem is what they evict.

---

## 2. Commit 0 — make the parked counts exact (do this first)

Two separate counters track parked lines, and **both lose events when two things happen in one cycle.**
Today that is rare. Commits 1–4 make guest evictions routine, so it stops being rare, and commit 3 turns
one of these counters into a **correctness** input. Fix both before anything else.

### 2.1 `parkCount` in the SetBalanceUnit — wrong set, not just a lost count

[Scheduler.scala:689-694](../../../design/craft/inclusivecache/src/Scheduler.scala#L689-L694):

```scala
sbu.io.dispRelease := mshrs.map(_.io.dispRelease).reduce(_ || _)
sbu.io.dispDrop    := mshrs.map(_.io.dispDrop).reduce(_ || _)
val dispOH = VecInit(mshrs.map(m => m.io.dispRelease || m.io.dispDrop)).asUInt
sbu.io.dispHome := Mux1H(dispOH, mshrs.map(_.io.dispHome))
assert (PopCount(dispOH) <= 1.U, "SBC: two MSHRs reclaimed a parked line in one cycle")
```

Two MSHRs reclaiming a guest in the same cycle give **one** decrement, applied to the **bitwise OR of the
two home-set numbers** — sets 5 and 3 become set 7, which lost nothing. The assert is simulation-only.

**Required fix: arbitrate, do not drop.** Each MSHR holds its erase event in a 1-bit pending register
with its `dispHome` value latched; the Scheduler grants **one per cycle** (priority encoder over the
pending bits) and acks that MSHR, which clears its bit. No event is lost and none is misattributed.
A small FIFO in the Scheduler is an acceptable alternative **only if it cannot silently drop**.

- A delayed decrement is safe in both directions: `mayHold` stays true one cycle longer (a wasted search)
  and teardown fires one cycle later. Never the other way.
- **Do not route the delayed path into `PerfCounters`.** `SBC_DispRelease` / `SBC_DispDrop` are already
  exact there (`PopCount`, [Scheduler.scala:758-759](../../../design/craft/inclusivecache/src/Scheduler.scala#L758-L759));
  they must keep counting the raw pulses on the cycle they happen.
- Keep an assert on the granted path: at most one grant per cycle, and a granted MSHR's pending bit
  must actually be set.
- **Same pattern, lower stakes, fix it the same way while you are here:**
  [Scheduler.scala:623-626](../../../design/craft/inclusivecache/src/Scheduler.scala#L623-L626) (`migReject`
  → DSS block list). Losing one is performance-only, but it is the same bug.

### 2.2 `SBC_Parked` in PerfCounters — under-counts by exactly the amount that matters

[PerfCounters.scala:233-237](../../../design/craft/inclusivecache/src/PerfCounters.scala#L233-L237):

```scala
val parkInc = p.migCommit =/= 0.U
val parkDec = p.dispRelease =/= 0.U || p.dispDrop =/= 0.U
when (parkInc && !parkDec)                        { parked := parked + 1.U }
.elsewhen (!parkInc && parkDec && parked =/= 0.U) { parked := parked - 1.U }
```

`p.dispRelease` and `p.dispDrop` are `PopCount`s — they can be 2 — but the level moves by **1**. Two
guests evicted in one cycle subtract one. So `SBC_Parked` **drifts upward**, and it is the headline number
for this whole experiment.

Replace with arithmetic on the counts, clamped at 0:

```scala
val inc = p.migCommit
val dec = p.dispRelease + p.dispDrop
parked := Mux(dec > parked + inc, 0.U, parked + inc - dec)
```

**This very likely explains finding F8 in the 005 report** (`SBC_Parked` ending 340–376 above
`migrations − dispRelease − dispDrop`, same sign, unexplained). Say so in `REPORT.md` if your numbers
agree, and **re-check whether the 477–483 parked figure was itself inflated** — it is the number the
fix is being judged against.

### 2.3 Check for commit 0

`migration_stress_test` 7/7, 0 asserts, on `VerilatorRocket8KL116KL2Config` and
`…NoSbcConfig`; `sbc_migrate_switch_test` passes. Every counter identical to the `sbc-start-2026-09-16`
run **except** `SBC_Parked`, which may now be lower. If it changes, say by how much — that is a result,
not a regression.

## 3. No new register — build the behaviour

**Decided 2026-09-16: do not add a runtime policy register, and do not build switchable variants of any of
these rules.** Three of the four changes below *delete* logic (a mask, two fallback tiers, a guard term);
only the cap adds anything, and that is one comparator. A register with four fields and a mux per rule
would cost more hardware than the fix itself and make every path harder to read.

What this means for you:

- **Each rule is simply the new behaviour.** No mux, no "old way" kept alive beside the new way.
- **The one tunable is a compile-time parameter**, in the same place as the existing SBC knobs
  (`InclusiveCacheMicroParameters`, [Parameters.scala:~117](../../../design/craft/inclusivecache/src/Parameters.scala#L117)):

  | Param | Default | Meaning |
  |---|---|---|
  | `guestCap` | `2` | Most guests one pairing may park in its partner. `0` = no cap, no hardware |

  Changing it is a rebuild, like `migrationThreshold` or `dssEntries`. Sweeping it is not this task.
- **The on/off comparison still works on one bitstream.** `SBC_MigrateEnable` (`0x3C0`, task 006) gives
  the migrate-off half and is untouched by everything here. The old-rules numbers are already measured —
  two board sessions on 2026-09-15/16, 005 REPORT "Board runs" — so nothing needs a switch to compare
  against.
- **What we give up, and accept:** on the board the four changes arrive as one combined result. The
  per-change direction comes from the simulation gate after each commit instead, which is why §8 asks for
  the same five numbers at every step.
- No `sw/sbc_mmio.h` / `sbc_read.c` register work, and no change to `run_board_session.exp`.

---

## 4. Commit 1 — C1, guests can be evicted

**Paper:** §2.2 — eviction is by recency. A guest inserted as MRU ages out and is then evicted like
anything else. There is no category exemption anywhere in the paper.

**Where:** the victim mux, [Directory.scala:216-226](../../../design/craft/inclusivecache/src/Directory.scala#L216-L226).

Today: tier 3 is the random pick masked to `nonDisplacedOH`; tier 4 takes the **first** home way when the
random pick lands on a guest; tier 5 takes a guest only when there is no home way at all.

**New behaviour: a guest is an ordinary candidate.** The random tier picks from **every** way:

```scala
Mux((lfsrVictimOH & freeWays).orR, lfsrVictimOH & freeWays,
    PriorityEncoderOH(freeWays))
```

- `nonDisplacedOH` and `displacedOH` are no longer needed for victim choice. **Delete the two fallback
  tiers with them** — the "take the first home way" tier and the "only now take a guest" tier both exist
  solely because the masked random tier can return nothing. That fallback was "Problem B" in the 09-11
  workplan (it fired on ~44% of evictions and made eviction non-random); it disappears rather than being
  fixed. **This is a net deletion of logic.**
- Tiers 1 and 2 (`preferInvalid`, `preferEvictable`) and the `freeWays` mask are unchanged and still come
  first. The `PopCount(victimWayOH) === 1` assert must still hold.
- Keep the comment block above the old mask, corrected rather than deleted: it records *why* guests were
  protected, and that reasoning is now the bug (3 lines, per the repo's comment rule).
- This puts the parked-victim release path (leftover **L2**, "only ever proven in a forced test") under
  real load for the first time. That is intentional, and it is the main thing the simulation gate is
  checking.

---

## 5. Commit 2 — C2, a migration may take an older guest's slot

**Paper:** §3.3 — *"If there is a miss, the LRU line of the destination set will be evicted, and the LRU
line from the source set will be moved to the destination set to replace it."* D's victim is its LRU line,
guest or home line alike.

**Two places must agree:**

1. **The directory must be allowed to offer a guest as the victim.** `evictableOH`
   ([Directory.scala:~197](../../../design/craft/inclusivecache/src/Directory.scala#L197)) excludes
   displaced ways. Add a new read flag `allowDisplacedVictim` to `DirectoryRead` and relax the term to
   `(!displaced || allowDisplacedVictim)`. It is a plain wire per read site, not a register.
   **The flag is `true.B` only on the destination probe** (`MSHR.scala:604-607`, the `!doSearch` dread), never
   on the source-side read. A source read must never pick a guest: migrating a guest a second time breaks
   the AT, which records one hop only.
2. **The MSHR must accept it.** `dstEvictable`
   ([MSHR.scala:1468-1470](../../../design/craft/inclusivecache/src/MSHR.scala#L1468-L1470))
   loses the `!io.directory.bits.displaced` term — one term deleted. **Keep `!dirty && !clients.orR`** — the slot is then
   taken by the same silent overwrite the code already performs for a clean, client-free home line. No new
   release path, no new MSHR state.

**Parked accounting must net to zero.** Under strict 1:1 pinning the guest being replaced belongs to the
same S that is migrating, so one guest leaves and one arrives. Carry a `reusedGuestSlot` bit on the commit
bundle and use it to suppress **both** the `parkCount` increment in the SBU and the `SBC_Parked`
increment in PerfCounters. Suppressing one and not the other is a silent drift.

**Out of scope on purpose:** taking a *dirty* or *client-held* guest. That needs a real Release from the
migrating MSHR at the guest's home address. Same class as leftover L5. Do not build it.

---

## 6. Commit 3 — C3, teardown

**Paper:** §3.4 — *"A disassociation can take place upon a first search miss (i.e., a native miss) in a
destination set i. If the OR of the d bits of this set changes from 1 to 0 as result of the eviction
triggered by the miss, the association is broken… The disassociation requires accessing the AT of the
source set of the association, as provided by AT(i).index, and clearing the association there."*

**Use `parkCount`, not `displacedOther`.** `parkCount(S) == 0` is the same predicate ("no guests of S are
parked anywhere") with no new directory signal and no read-to-eviction timing window. `displacedOther`
([Directory.scala:303](../../../design/craft/inclusivecache/src/Directory.scala#L303)) stays unused.

In the SBU, at the decrement: when it takes `parkCount(decSet)` from 1 to 0, clear
`at(decSet)` **and** `at(at(decSet).assocSet)`. Both sets re-enter the DSS on their own — `dss.io.update`
already admits any set whose AT entry is invalid
([SetBalanceUnit.scala:124](../../../design/craft/inclusivecache/src/SetBalanceUnit.scala#L124)), so no
new DSS port is needed.

**Two nets. This is the one dangerous corner of the task; neither may be a comment.**

- **N1 — do not tear down a pairing a live migration is using.** Gate on `anyMigrating`
  ([Scheduler.scala:281](../../../design/craft/inclusivecache/src/Scheduler.scala#L281)), which must be
  brought into the SBU. Only one migration exists at a time, so no other pairing can be written while it
  is in flight — but its own commit would re-pair sets you just cleared. If the teardown is blocked, hold
  it in a 1-deep pending register and retry; if that register is already occupied, drop the second
  teardown (the pair simply stays, which is safe) and **count it**, so we can see if it ever matters.
- **N2 — an in-flight second search must re-validate its pairing.** After a teardown, D can be paired to
  a different source S2 and receive S2's guests. A searcher from S that latched `pairSetReg = D` earlier
  could then tag-match **S2's** guest and serve the wrong address. On the cycle the search result
  arrives, compare the live `io.pairInfo` (already keyed to the MSHR receiving the directory result — the
  002 C1 fix) against the latched `pairValidReg` / `pairSetReg` / `pairIsSrcReg`. On a mismatch, treat it
  as a **secondary miss** (safe: `parkCount == 0` means there was nothing of S's to find, so the refetch
  is correct) and fire a sim-only assert so we learn it happened.

---

## 7. Commit 4 — C4, cap the guests per pairing

**Not in the paper as a rule — it is the paper's measured result.** The paper reports **2.15 lines
displaced per pairing**, i.e. one or two guests resident in D at a time out of K=16 ways. Its LRU produces
that on its own; our random replacement cannot, so we state it (fix plan §2 has the arithmetic).

- `guestCap` is the compile-time parameter from §3, default **2**. When it is `0`, Scala-gate the whole
  thing away so that no comparator is elaborated at all.
- In the SBU, add `parkFull := parkCount(io.assocQuery.bits) >= guestCap.U` to the **existing**
  `assocResp` bundle. It uses the same index as `mayHold`, so there is **no new sets-wide mux** — do not
  add one.
- The MSHR latches it with the rest of `pairInfo` on the directory result and refuses to start a
  migration while it is set.
- A refusal is an existing "declined before start", so it lands in `SBC_Aborted` as those already do
  (CLAUDE.md register table). `SBC_Declined` belongs to task 005 commit 2 and is not being built.

## 8. Tests

Existing gate, unchanged, after **every** commit: `migration_stress_test` 7/7 with 0 asserts on
`VerilatorRocket8KL116KL2Config` and `…NoSbcConfig`, `sbc_migrate_switch_test` T1–T4, both shadow
checkers quiet, run through `make run-binary` (never a bare `$SIM`).

Two new cases in `sw/migration_stress_test.c`, both needing `sbcForceDstSet` so one destination row can
be filled. Both are behaviour tests now, not switch tests — there is no switch to flip:

- **T-CAP** — force one destination and drive many migrations. The guests parked out of one source must
  never exceed `guestCap`. Build once with `guestCap = 1` (easiest to see), then confirm the default of 2
  behaves the same way at 2.
- **T-TEARDOWN** — park lines, then touch the destination set until every guest is gone. Read
  `SBC_SetSel` / `SBC_Status` bit 2 for both sets: **both must report unpaired**. This is the first test
  this project has ever had for pairing teardown.

**Report the same five numbers after every commit** — `SBC_Parked` at the end, `SBC_Migrations`,
`L2_PrimaryHit`, `L2_SecondaryHit`, `L2_DataMiss`, and the hit rate from
[cache-terminology.md](../../guides/cache-terminology.md). With no runtime switch, this per-commit
sequence is the **only** per-change evidence we get, so do not skip it on a commit that "obviously"
changes nothing.

## 10. Do not

- **Do not** add a check on the destination's saturation before each displacement. The paper measured
  that and it was worse (§3.2: 0.6% worse miss rate, 0.38% worse IPC). Our current behaviour is correct.
- **Do not** change how the saturation counters are updated on a partner hit. Settled 2026-09-16 against
  the paper's Figures 2 and 3 — our home `+1` matches, and the missing partner `−1` changes no decision
  while two sets are paired.
- **Do not** weaken any `w.displaced` test in the hit path. Two ways matching one tag is the stale-twin
  hole; `Directory.scala:246` asserts it for a reason.
- **Do not** let a source-side read pick a guest as a migration victim (§5).
- **Do not** build task 005 commits 2 or 3, a replacement-policy change (PLRU is a separate decision), or
  dirty-guest handling.
- **Do not** add a control register, a runtime switch, or a "keep the old behaviour too" mux for any of
  these rules. Decided 2026-09-16 — see §3. If you believe a change cannot be made without one, stop and
  say so in `REPORT.md` rather than building it.
- **Do not** fix anything you find that is outside this task. Write it in `REPORT.md` under Findings —
  that is how F7, F8 and F9 were caught last time.
